subject: Post-demo: HealthEdge security follow-up — PT handback, vuln SLA & scan cadence
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@healthedge.com>, Greg Patterson <greg.patterson@healthedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Recap + next steps from today's demo (security items)

Hi Alice / Greg —

Thanks for a great demo call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on security/compliance items we discussed so your security team can evaluate Redwood for the HealthEdge integration: 

- SOC 2: you said you wanted details on our Type II coverage and timestamped artifacts. I can surface our SOC 2 summary and SOC auditor contact.
- Vendor questionnaire: you mentioned a short vendor security questionnaire (~30 Qs) you use for initial qualification. Please send the file or link; we can triage today.
- Penetration test (handback): you asked whether we can share past PT reports and our vulnerability management process.
- Remediation SLAs & scan cadence: we briefly touched on expectations — wanted to propose a concrete set of SLAs for discussion.

Proposed next steps / asks:
1) Can you upload your questionnaire (or confirm the link) so we can start answering?
2) If possible, please share a redacted copy of the most recent PT report (redacted for customer PII/keys) so our security team can validate scope and remediation history.
3) We'll propose a standard vulnerability SLA and scan cadence below; if that looks reasonable we can include it in the mutual action plan.

Redwood suggested baseline (for commercial engagements):
- Critical / exploitable RCEs: remediation or temporary mitigation within 7 business days
- High (privilege escalation, exposed credentials): remediation within 30 calendar days
- Medium: remediation within 90 calendar days
- Scanning cadence: external unauthenticated scans weekly; authenticated full scans quarterly; annual full PT by third party

I'll start a short MAM doc (one-pager) and paste the link once it's ready. If you prefer different SLA buckets we can adjust.

Thanks again — available for a 30-minute follow-up on Friday if that helps.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@healthedge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Greg Patterson <greg.patterson@healthedge.com>
Date: 2027-02-15T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's demo (security items)

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few answers from our side and one request: 

- SOC 2: HealthEdge requires SOC 2 Type II evidence for control design and operating effectiveness. We need your SOC 2 bridge letter and the auditor contact. Can you provide the latest artifacts (summary + point of contact)?
- Questionnaire: attaching our vendor questionnaire (HealthEdge-SecQ-2027.xlsx). Please have your security team fill the workbook and return.
- PT report: we can accept a redacted PT handback (remove customer PII, internal IP ranges that would identify our hosted envs, and any exploit PoCs). We asked our procurement team to share an NDA if necessary — copying Greg here.

One clarification on scope: for our security team to sign off we typically want:
  * Evidence of historical findings and remediation status for the last 18 months
  * Scan cadence & ownership (who runs authenticated scans vs. external scans)
  * Public disclosure policy for vulnerabilities (we have a coordinated disclosure expectation)

I'll upload the PT report to our SFTP for your team to pull once we confirm redaction level. Attaching the questionnaire now.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short technical sync next week if Marissa or your security lead want to run through the questionnaire live.

Regards,
Alice Nguyen
Director, Security & Compliance
HealthEdge
[Attachment: HealthEdge-SecQ-2027.xlsx (Excel, 46 KB)]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@healthedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-15T12:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's demo (security items)

Alice —

Appreciate the quick reply and for sending the questionnaire. We'll have Marissa's team start answers today; target to return a completed workbook by EOD Tue.

A couple quick commitments from Redwood to streamline evaluation and match your asks: 
- SOC 2 artifacts: I'll route our SOC 2 Type II summary and the auditor POC to you by EOD Monday.
- PT handback: we'll accept your redaction guidance. If HealthEdge can place the redacted report in the SFTP we can pull it; alternatively we can accept an upload to a shared Google Drive link.
- Proposed vulnerability SLA (confirmed): Critical 7 business days; High 30 calendar days; Medium 90 calendar days. If those targets are acceptable we'll reflect them in the MAM.
- Scan cadence we propose by default: weekly external scans (automated), quarterly authenticated scans (internal), and annual third-party PT with handback. Ownership: Redwood runs the authenticated scans; for external scans we can accept a joint team or provide reports from our scanning vendor.

Marissa — could your team confirm the redaction checklist we prefer for PT handback (PII, full exploit PoCs, customer network identifiers)? Also confirm whether we need a separate ATO for pulling the artifact from HealthEdge SFTP.

Jonas — loop back on timing for procurement and any negotiating levers (credits / shortened trial) tied to expedited security review.

Thanks,
Ben

Date: 2027-02-16T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's demo (security items)

Ben / team / Alice —

Thanks for the context. A few clarifications from Redwood Security: 

1) Redaction checklist for PT handback (HealthEdge should apply these before upload):
   - Remove any PII (usernames, email addresses, full names)
   - Remove internal IP ranges and customer-specific hostnames that could identify your production estate
   - Strip verbatim exploit PoC code; summarize the exploit and the affected component instead
   - Retain finding severity, evidence snapshots (screenshots w/ redaction), remediation status, and timestamps

2) Disclosure policy: Redwood supports coordinated disclosure. We ask partners to allow a 30-day remediation window for Critical findings before public disclosure, unless an immediate risk to customers requires otherwise. We will always follow an agreed disclosure plan documented in the MAM.

3) SLA alignment: the proposed buckets look reasonable. One operational ask: for Critical / exploitable findings we need a dedicated Slack channel or PagerDuty escalation contact so remediation steps can be coordinated in real time. If HealthEdge can provide a point of contact, we'll configure the escalation policy.

4) Document exchange: preferred mechanism is a secure SFTP or a transient Google Drive link with limited access and no public sharing. If HealthEdge needs us to sign an NDA for PT artifacts, we can circulate the standard Redwood mutual NDA (I can initiate).

Attaching: Redwood-PT-handback-guidance.pdf (internal template) — will provide to HealthEdge once we have confirmation on upload method.

Marissa Cole
Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
